title: Palbociclib with endocrine therapy
setting: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
dose: Usual palbociclib dose: 125 mg once daily on Days 1–21 of a 28-day cycle; reduced prescribed doses are 100 mg or 75 mg.
schedule: Take palbociclib for 21 days, then have 7 days without palbociclib. The aromatase-inhibitor tablet continues every day, or fulvestrant injections follow their separate schedule. The week off applies to palbociclib, not automatically to the hormone treatment.
administration: Check whether the pharmacy supplied capsules or tablets: capsules are taken with food; tablets can be taken with or without food. Swallow whole at a consistent time. Avoid grapefruit. If you miss or vomit a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Do not restart after a clinical hold until the treating team confirms.
duration: Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable. There is no fixed adjuvant course in NCCP 00414. Blood results or symptoms may change the dose or postpone the next cycle.
indication: NCCP 00414 a: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic disease with an aromatase inhibitor. NCCP 00414 b: the same receptor/disease setting with fulvestrant in women who have received prior endocrine therapy. Pre/perimenopausal women also need an agreed ovarian-suppression plan.
purpose: Palbociclib slows cell-cycle progression while the hormone partner reduces oestrogen signalling. The aim in this advanced-disease pathway is cancer control, with treatment and response reviewed over time.
baseline: Before the first dose: FBC, kidney and liver bloods; review other medicines, pregnancy possibility, receptor results, menopausal status and the exact endocrine partner. Confirm ovarian suppression when relevant.
ongoing: FBC on Day 1 and Day 15 of cycles 1–2, then Day 1 from cycle 3. Kidney/liver bloods before each cycle. If counts are low, extra blood tests and a pause may be needed. Only after no worse than grade 1/2 neutropenia in the first 6 cycles may FBC frequency reduce to every 3 months before a cycle, with additional tests when clinically indicated.
heart: Palbociclib does not have the routine ECG timetable used for ribociclib. ECG or echo is arranged if symptoms, another medicine or individual cardiac risk make it appropriate.
bone: Bone-health monitoring belongs to the endocrine partner, ovarian suppression and personal fracture risk. If taking an aromatase inhibitor, agree the baseline bone-density assessment and follow-up plan with the team; palbociclib itself has no fixed DXA interval.
urgent: Contact the treatment team promptly if you feel feverish or unwell, have shaking chills or infection symptoms, or develop new cough or breathlessness. Follow the local emergency temperature instructions; do not wait for a planned blood test or for the 38.5°C value used in one clinician dose-adjustment table. Severe breathing difficulty needs emergency care.
special: The same low count can lead to a different action at Day 1 and Day 15 of the first two cycles. Dose decisions also depend on fever/infection, recovery, severity and current dose. A clinician must confirm a restart; the patient timeline is an explanation, not permission to self-adjust treatment.
contraception: Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. EMA specifies effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose for women and 14 weeks for men; the endocrine partner may require a longer interval. Discuss fertility preservation before treatment when relevant.

logistics.title: Two treatments with different clocks
logistics.text: An aromatase inhibitor is taken continuously. If fulvestrant is the partner, the usual 500 mg injection schedule is Days 1, 15 and 29 initially, then every 28 days under NCCP scheduling. Injection dose and tolerability need their own clinical review. Ovarian-suppression injections, if needed, have another prescribed schedule.

logistics.title: The first two cycles need an extra blood test
logistics.text: The Day 15 blood count checks for early marrow suppression. A Day 22 repeat may be requested after a low Day 15 count. The team interprets the result and tells you whether to continue or pause.

logistics.title: The week off and next prescription
logistics.text: Days 22–28 are the planned palbociclib rest week. Arrange the next blood test and supply in advance. The team may draw pre-cycle bloods locally before Day 1; the exact appointment is a local arrangement, not a universal Day 25/26 rule.

logistics.title: New medicines and formulations
logistics.text: Tell the oncology pharmacist about antibiotics, antifungals, supplements and herbal medicines. Avoid St John’s Wort and grapefruit. Food instructions differ for capsules and tablets, so check the dispensed box.

logistics.title: Visits and access
logistics.text: Palbociclib itself is an oral treatment and does not require a port or infusion pump. Fulvestrant or ovarian-suppression partners require injection visits. Do not infer that these visits stop during the palbociclib rest week.

support.title: Nausea support
support.text: Palbociclib is classified as oral minimal–low emetic risk. Routine premedication is not usually needed; discuss rescue medication if nausea occurs. A generic intensive chemotherapy antiemetic schedule is not automatically added.

support.title: Low counts and infection
support.text: Blood-count monitoring, dose interruption and dose reduction are central to support. Growth-factor use is an individual clinical decision, not an automatic routine injection on this card.

support.title: Hormone-related symptoms
support.text: Discuss hot flushes, joint symptoms, vaginal symptoms, sleep and bone health according to the actual endocrine partner. Support can be adjusted without silently changing either cancer medicine.

support.title: Mouth, bowel and energy symptoms
support.text: Report mouth soreness, troublesome nausea/diarrhoea or fatigue so supportive treatment and hydration can be reviewed. New breathing symptoms must not be dismissed as expected fatigue.

agents.name: Palbociclib
agents.mechanism: Blocks cell-cycle signals that help cancer cells divide
agents.explanation: Hormone signalling can activate cyclin-D/CDK4/6. Palbociclib blocks this control point, helping keep susceptible cells from progressing through the cell cycle. Combining it with endocrine therapy acts on both the hormonal signal and downstream cell division.
agents.watch: The key early issue is a falling white-cell count, which may cause no symptoms. Keep blood-test appointments and report infection symptoms or new cough/breathlessness promptly.
risks: Rare but serious interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis

agents.name: Your endocrine partner
agents.type: Either an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant
agents.mechanism: Reduces oestrogen signalling to hormone-sensitive cells
visual: AI lowers oestrogen; fulvestrant targets its receptor
agents.explanation: An aromatase inhibitor lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant acts at the oestrogen receptor. These are alternative partners here, not an instruction to take both. The partner’s dose, monitoring and injection or tablet schedule must be confirmed.
agents.watch: Discuss joint/hot-flush and bone symptoms with an AI, or injection-site/bleeding symptoms with fulvestrant. Pre/perimenopausal women require ovarian suppression in the prescribed combination.
risks: Hot flushes and other hormone-related symptoms
AI: joint symptoms and bone loss
Partner-specific liver, interaction and pregnancy considerations

evidence.title: PALOMA-2, palbociclib + letrozole: EMA efficacy tables 6 and 8
evidence.population: 666 postmenopausal patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without prior systemic treatment for advanced disease; 444 palbociclib/letrozole vs 222 placebo/letrozole.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Investigator-assessed PFS at the 2016 primary analysis: 24.8 vs 14.5 months; HR 0.576 (95% CI 0.463–0.718).
evidence.interpretation: Adding palbociclib delayed progression in the studied population.
evidence.limitations: PFS is not survival. Final overall survival was not statistically significant: 53.9 vs 51.2 months; HR 0.956 (95% CI 0.777–1.177), p=0.6755, cutoff 15 November 2021. Do not present this as a proven OS benefit.

evidence.title: PALOMA-3, palbociclib + fulvestrant: EMA efficacy table 9
evidence.population: 521 patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced cancer after endocrine progression; 347 palbociclib/fulvestrant vs 174 placebo/fulvestrant, with ovarian suppression for pre/perimenopausal women.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Updated investigator-assessed PFS, 23 October 2015 cutoff: 11.2 vs 4.6 months; HR 0.497 (95% CI 0.398–0.620).
evidence.interpretation: Adding palbociclib improved PFS after prior endocrine therapy.
evidence.limitations: The prespecified final OS analysis was not statistically significant: 34.9 vs 28.0 months; HR 0.814 (95% CI 0.644–1.029). Separate later exploratory follow-up from this final analysis; do not compare PFS numerically with PALOMA-2 as if populations matched.

cycle_rows.text: No palbociclib; next cycle only after team confirmation

cycle_rows.label: Endocrine partner
cycle_rows.text: AI every day OR fulvestrant at its scheduled injection visits

cycle_rows.label: Blood-count changes
cycle_rows.text: May occur without symptoms. FBC Day 1 and Day 15 of first 2 cycles; extra tests if low.

cycle_rows.label: Symptoms vary between people
cycle_rows.text: Mouth soreness, nausea or fatigue can occur; no guaranteed day-by-day prediction.

clinical_notes: Patient schedule is relative and requires no date input. It does not authorise treatment or restart.
NCCP v 5 a capsule instructions require food. EMA includes tablets that allow food or no food; confirm formulation rather than silently generalising.
NCCP expects no renal reduction in dialysis; EMA has insufficient dialysis data. Explicit oncology/pharmacy review is retained, with no invented numeric reduction.
Grade 3 atDay 1 andDay 15 ofcycles 1–2 have different actions. Isolated grade 3 count without timing returns review; it does not force unrelated inputs.
Fever/infection grading input means grade 3 neutropenia plus fever≥38.5°C and/or infection. Patient fever instructions must follow local safety-netting, not wait for 38.5°C.
No routine palbociclib-only ECG, echo, fixed 3 monthly CT or tumour-marker schedule is mandated by NCCP.
All clinical-use, consultant-validation and oncology-pharmacy-validation flags remain false.
